newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Charges seen dragging BT Q2 profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Charges seen dragging BT Q2 profit.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) is due to turn in lower second quarter pre-tax profits next Thursday, with earnings depressed by a 200 million stg redundancy charge and the repayment of government debt.

Analysts said they had pencilled in pre-tax profits of around 670-710 million stg, a fall of about seven percent from the 732 million stg a year ago. In the half year, expectations range from 1.5 billion-1.6 billion stg and following company predictions, analysts are awaiting a 7.9p half year dividend.
BT's $20 billion merger with MCI of the U.S., to form one of the world's largest telephone groups, is seen as broadly neutral for the company in the longer term.
Some analysts say the synergy benefits will roughly offset a 30 percent premium that BT will have to pay for a deal that will dilute earnings by five percent in its first year.

In the meantime, analysts will be looking for any hints from BT on the growth of its fixed lines business, new redundancies and guidance on some of its European joint ventures such as Cegetel in France or Viag Interkom in Germany.
Analysts said they were also seeking any news on the extent to which BT's business line growth has been affected by the growing cable sector.
Having had time to digest the implications of the move, most industry analysts welcomed BT's decision to snap up the rest of MCI, in which it had held a 20 percent stake since 1993.

But some questioned company projections that the new telecoms giant, dubbed Concert Plc, would see double-digit growth -- news that had helped prompt some buy recommendations on BT's stock up to 400 pence.
On Friday, the stock was trading at 365-1/2, a gain of 2p.

"I don't believe this company (Concert) is going to grow more than eight or nine percent a year," said Andrew Harrington, telecoms analyst at Salomon Brothers, adding that he thought BT's current share price was fairly valued.

"It always made sense for BT to buy the rest of MCI...I was just surprised they did it when they did. I thought they would first concentrate on Europe and perhaps Japan. "But I don't think it's going to alter my view that BT, in its home UK market, is not going to grow at all in the next five years and that's what that 8-9 percent growth represents."

The benefits from the deal, estimated by BT at 500 million stg pre-tax per year, will only flow through in the fifth year after completion. But that is only expected towards the end of next year if the merger wins U.S. and UK regulatory approval.

BT has underperformed the FTSE All Share index since June 95 by 20 percent and underperformed the telecoms sector by about six percent, according to a relative performance study in Reuters 3000 analytics.
With growing competition in its home market as well as abroad, tariffs are expected to be increasingly driven down, eating into BT's market share.
"In my view, BT's profits on a stand alone basis will be flat to down in the next few years," said Harrington.

BT's current price earnings ratio is around 11.6 compared to Cable and Wireless' 17.56 and mobile phone group Vodafone's 24.24 and against a sector PE of nearly 21, according to Reuters Securities 3000 analytics.
